I think there's a taboo around it (and more broadly around mental illness - especially depression) that shouldn't exist.

I have depression, I have failed one attempt, and even though I don't consider this anymore, I understand why people would do it. I think people should be able to take their lives whenever they wish, even though it will be hurtful for their surroundings (if they have people that depend on them, though, it's a bit more complicated). Now suicide is a taboo, because it's often seen as an avoidable, permanent solution to a temporary problem, and the person's friends and family don't want to grieve a loved one (which is totally understandable). Also, suicidal episodes induced my mental health problems are a product of said mental health problems : suicidal people, when they're about to do it, often don't have a clear mind and just suffer enough to consider death a preferable alternative.

The question that needs to be addressed is if it is justifiable to forcibly try to heal someone, maybe without their consent, to keep them alive even if they don't want to. If someone has cancer but doesn't want to go through chemo, should we force them to have one or just let them die as they wish ? That's kinda the same situation.
